title: SafeMT: Multi-turn Safety for Multimodal Language Models
findings: The paper does not provide specific findings for religion alone, but for the broader category of 'Satire' which includes religious beliefs. It found that most Multimodal Language Models (MLLMs) do not refuse to generate satirical content until they detect bias or discrimination. Consequently, when dialogues are employed to prompt the models to generate satirical responses, the Attack Success Rate (ASR) decreases compared to when prompts are more direct.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the model's safety in scenarios involving 'Bias' and 'Satire'. For 'Bias', it assesses the generation of content with unfair stereotypes or discriminatory views based on religion. For 'Satire', it evaluates whether the model generates content that mocks or ridicules religious beliefs in a harmful way.
